name: claude-placeholder-config
purpose: The same empty-messages arm as claude-empty-placeholder, but with 'promptPlaceholder' SET in config.yaml, which proves the module-load read at prompt-converters.js:4 actually consults the runtime config rather than always using "Let's get started.". DISCRIMINATING BECAUSE: this recording and claude-empty-placeholder's use the SAME request body and differ only in that config line, so the recorded text must differ between them -- a body carrying the default here would mean the config was ignored.
stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.

tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend. Justified by tools/mock-provider listening on port 0.
tier2.harnessSource: tools/mock-provider/main.go: --port 0 asks the kernel for a free port, so the authority is not stable

tier2.rule: value replaced with <redacted>, presence and name preserved
tier2.reason: CLAUDE authenticates with x-api-key, NOT an Authorization header, so the bearer redaction does not reach it. The scenario declares the key and the harness asserts it arrived; only the value is dropped from the record.

tier2.rule: the recorder origin is replaced with <mock>
tier2.reason: The pinned leg reaches the recorder through the probe transport redirect and the Go leg through its seam, because API_CLAUDE is a pinned literal. The PATH (/messages, and its normalization) is untouched and IS compared.
tier2.pinnedSource: src/endpoints/backends/chat-completions.js:74 API_CLAUDE = https://api.anthropic.com/v1, :231 new URL(reverse_proxy || API_CLAUDE).toString(), :410 apiUrl + /messages

tier3.reason: It is a measurement of elapsed wall-clock time, so it differs on every run and no backend can match it; the value is a duration, not a contract.
